newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends higher after late rally.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends higher after late rally.

text.p: COMEX copper shrugged off earlier lows amid rising LME stocks to bounce back and close up on the day.
"It was a shortcovering blast that came out of both COMEX and LME. It was a delayed reaction to damp squib of a July LME options expiration," Richard Hirsch of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said.
There was no fundamental news behind the advance which came on light volume.
The copper market was on edge in the run-up to the options expiry, with some traders expecting a bumpy ride. The non-event, coupled with another rise in LME stocks, led to an early technical selloff.
A recovery in LME zinc and aluminum prompted copper to recover later, Hirsch said.
September COMEX settled up 1.85 cents at 111.90 cents a lb, traded 112.10 to 108.50 cents. Spot July went out 1.45 cents higher at 113.60 cents.
The active September to December spread widened a cent to over 3.00 cents. The LME cash to three months backwardation widened to $145/$155 a tonne, up from about $122 overnight.
LME stocks rose 1,750 tonnes to 130,075 tonnes.
Meanwhile, the auto industry, a key copper consumer, reported falling vehicle sales in June. Chrysler said late Tuesday that U.S light vehicle sales fell 4 percent compared to a year ago.
Wednesday, General Motors said June car sales fell 16.7 percent, and were down 9.5 percent January through June.
Prudential Securities said in a report it expected a world copper market deficit of 116,000 short tons this year, switching to a surplus of 604,300 short tons in 1998 which could continue into 1999.
"Note that this marks the first major and prolonged period in the past 20 years that the market almost totally ignored a pending oversupply situation," Prudential said.
"Coupled with this are some questionable trading procedures and the use of private warehouses to store copper stocks, which are not reported to regulatory bodies," Prudential added.
